To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MRAS speed estimator can be used to improve the performance of the vector controlled IM drive.
the MRAS-based vector control method is more efficient than the conventional method in terms of the dynamic performance of the system.

1) MRAS based sensorless speed estimator for vector controlled induction motor drive is proposed; 2) The proposed method is robust and is immune to the stator resistance variation; 3) A single current sensor based drive is formulated; 4) A new speed estimator based on the current model reference adaptive system (CMRAS) is proposed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for speed and current estimation of a vector controlled induction motor drive.
a new approach for speed estimation of an induction machine.
the design of an adaptive control scheme that can achieve robustness and stability in the presence of uncertainties and disturbances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MRAS based vector controlled induction motor drive with single current sensor is a viable alternative to speed sensor based drive.
this paper has presented a single current sensor vector controlled speed sensorless induction motor drive with MRAS based speed and current estimation technique.
MRAS-based sensorless control of the induction motor is a promising technique.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a speed sensorless vector control induction motor drive is presented with the help of MRAS.
the speed estimation is based on the MRAS and current estimation is done using the synchronous reference frame variables.
the proposed method is a simple and effective way to implement a vector controlled drive with single current sensor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single current sensor vector control can be realized by using MRAS and current estimation techniques.
the MRAS based speed estimator is a very simple and robust method for speed estimation.
we can estimate the speed of an induction motor without a speed sensor.
